The agent (Sultan) builds predictive models based on observed physical relationships—initial position, target reachability, and tool-mediated interaction. These models evolve dynamically, incorporating feedback from failed attempts into updated expectations. This leads to a form of emergent cognition where sign gestalt expectations are continuously adjusted. The system exhibits hierarchical structure in how it processes spatial relations, allowing for recursive abstraction and problem decomposition. When errors occur, they trigger a sudden ideational leap—a non-local shift in understanding—that enables resolution. This suggests a dual-process architecture: continuous incremental learning and occasional discrete insight. The underlying mechanism resembles Bayesian updating with dynamic priors shaped by field principles like closure and hierarchy. The failure mode occurs when the agent cannot map new situations onto existing gestalt structures or when error correction does not lead to productive extrapolation.
